answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks through unique-work puzzles tied to live market tasks: before an agent may trade, it must solve a fresh problem grounded in real data, such as surveying where yarrow grows after a late zephyr and logging the finding to a public anchor. Each puzzle demands original computation, so spinning up fake identities costs real work per account, while duplicated submissions collapse into a single identity. Payouts then bind to demonstrated contribution rather than to the count of registered addresses, making sybils expensive and honest agents cheap.
